title: What Is an OpenAI-Compatible API and How to Use One
description: What an OpenAI-compatible API is and how to use one: base URL, key and model, with Python, JavaScript and curl code, env vars and common error fixes.
author: freellm.site
content:
An **OpenAI-compatible API** is an LLM endpoint that accepts the same requests and returns the same responses as OpenAI's `chat/completions` API. Because the format matches, the official OpenAI SDKs work against it once you change three values: the **base URL**, the **API key**, and the **model name**. Most free LLM providers work this way, so one codebase can run on Groq, Gemini, Mistral, Cerebras and others.

Below is how the pattern works, with working code in Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and curl. It also covers switching providers with environment variables, which features carry over and which don't, and how to fix the errors you're most likely to hit. If you only need a list of compatible providers, see our [drop-in list of OpenAI-compatible free LLM APIs](/blog/openai-compatible-free-llm-apis-list/).

*Every base URL and model name below was checked against each provider's official docs in September 2026. Models get retired often, so the fixes section shows how to confirm a model ID yourself.*

## What does "OpenAI-compatible" mean?

It means the provider copied OpenAI's **HTTP interface**. OpenAI's models are not involved. A compatible provider exposes the same paths, most importantly:

- `POST {base_url}/chat/completions`: send a `messages` array, get back a `choices` array
- `GET {base_url}/models`: list the model IDs the provider serves

The request body uses the same field names (`model`, `messages`, `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `stream`, `tools`, `response_format`). The response uses the same shape (`choices[0].message.content`, `usage.prompt_tokens`, and so on). Your parsing code doesn't need to know which company answered.

Compatibility comes in degrees. Most providers match the core chat endpoint closely, then differ on extras such as embeddings, vision input, logprobs, or how many completions (`n`) you can request per call. Groq, for example, [documents its unsupported fields](https://console.groq.com/docs/openai): `logprobs`, `logit_bias`, `top_logprobs`, `messages[].name`, and any `n` other than 1. Google [labels its OpenAI support as beta](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai). Treat compatibility as "the basics work everywhere". Test the advanced features on each provider before you rely on them.

## How does it work? Base URL, API key, model

An OpenAI SDK client needs three pieces of information, and each one maps to something the provider controls:

| Setting | What it is | Example (Groq) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `base_url` | The provider's API root. The SDK appends `/chat/completions` to it | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` |
| `api_key` | Your key from the provider's console, sent as `Authorization: Bearer ...` | `gsk_...` |
| `model` | A model ID the provider actually serves | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` |

By default the SDK sends requests to `https://api.openai.com/v1`. When you set `base_url`, the same request goes to the provider instead. Your OpenAI key won't work there, so you use the provider's key. And the provider doesn't host `gpt-4o`, so you pick a model from its own catalog.

Keep the full base URL, including the path. It usually ends in `/v1`, but not always. Gemini's is `.../v1beta/openai/` and Groq's includes `/openai/v1`. Drop that path and you get a 404.

If you don't have a key yet, our guide to [getting a free LLM API key without a credit card](/blog/how-to-get-free-llm-api-key-no-credit-card/) covers the signup flow for each provider.

## Python example (openai SDK)

Install the official SDK with `pip install openai`, then point the client at a free provider. This example uses [Groq](/providers/groq/), whose free plan currently allows 30 requests per minute and 1,000 requests per day on `openai/gpt-oss-120b` ([Groq rate limits](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits)).

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1",
    api_key=os.environ["GROQ_API_KEY"],
)

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": "Explain what a base URL is in one sentence."},
    ],
)

print(response.choices[0].message.content)
print(response.usage)  # token counts, same shape as OpenAI
```

Streaming works the same way it does against OpenAI. Pass `stream=True` and read the deltas:

```python
stream = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Count to five."}],
    stream=True,
)
for chunk in stream:
    if chunk.choices and chunk.choices[0].delta.content:
        print(chunk.choices[0].delta.content, end="", flush=True)
```

Use the **Chat Completions** API (`client.chat.completions`), not OpenAI's newer Responses API (`client.responses`). Chat Completions is the interface free providers copy. Support for the Responses API varies much more.

## JavaScript / TypeScript example (openai npm)

Install with `npm install openai`. The Node SDK spells the option `baseURL` and the key `apiKey`. This example uses [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) through its [OpenAI compatibility layer](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai):

```typescript
import OpenAI from "openai";

const client = new OpenAI({
  baseURL: "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/",
  apiKey: process.env.GEMINI_API_KEY,
});

const completion = await client.chat.completions.create({
  model: "gemini-3.8-flash",
  messages: [
    { role: "system", content: "You are a concise assistant." },
    { role: "user", content: "Give me three uses for an LLM API." },
  ],
});

console.log(completion.choices[0].message.content);
```

The same file runs as plain JavaScript in an ES module (`"type": "module"` in `package.json`), because top-level `await` needs ESM. For streaming, add `stream: true` and loop with `for await (const chunk of stream)`. Each chunk exposes `chunk.choices[0]?.delta?.content`, the same as in Python.

## curl example

With curl you can see exactly what the SDKs send, which is useful when a request fails and you want to rule out the library. This example calls [Cerebras](/providers/cerebras/) ([OpenAI compatibility docs](https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/resources/openai)):

```bash
curl https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CEREBRAS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-oss-120b",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "What is an OpenAI-compatible API?"}
    ]
  }'
```

Before you guess at a model name, list the valid ones:

```bash
curl https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CEREBRAS_API_KEY"
```

Every provider in the table below supports `GET /models`, and that response is the source of truth for model IDs. It's more reliable than blog posts, including this one.

## How to switch providers with environment variables

Don't hardcode the base URL. Both official SDKs read two environment variables when you construct the client with no arguments: `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_BASE_URL`. The [Python SDK](https://github.com/openai/openai-python) and the [Node SDK](https://github.com/openai/openai-node) both fall back to `OPENAI_BASE_URL` when you don't pass a base URL.

```bash
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://api.groq.com/openai/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-groq-key"
export LLM_MODEL="openai/gpt-oss-120b"
```

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()  # picks up OPENAI_BASE_URL and OPENAI_API_KEY
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model=os.environ["LLM_MODEL"],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}],
)
```

The model name has no standard variable, so add one of your own (`LLM_MODEL` above). Otherwise a provider switch still means a code edit.

For apps that fail over between providers, a small config map works better than one global client:

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

PROVIDERS = {
    "groq": ("https://api.groq.com/openai/v1", "GROQ_API_KEY", "openai/gpt-oss-120b"),
    "cerebras": ("https://api.cerebras.ai/v1", "CEREBRAS_API_KEY", "gpt-oss-120b"),
    "gemini": ("https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/", "GEMINI_API_KEY", "gemini-3.8-flash"),
}

def make_client(name: str) -> tuple[OpenAI, str]:
    base_url, key_var, model = PROVIDERS[name]
    return OpenAI(base_url=base_url, api_key=os.environ[key_var]), model

client, model = make_client(os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER", "groq"))
```

Now a rate limit on one free tier is a one-variable change (`LLM_PROVIDER=cerebras`). You can also catch the error and retry on the next provider. The same variables configure many developer tools too. See [using a free LLM API in Cursor, Claude Code and other AI tools](/blog/use-free-llm-api-cursor-claude-code/).

## What is (and isn't) compatible?

Plain chat requests (messages in, text out) work on every provider below. Past that, support depends on the provider and often on the specific model. Here is how the common features compare:

| Feature | How portable it is | What to watch for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Chat completions** | Works everywhere | Some fields are ignored or rejected (`logprobs`, `n > 1` on Groq and Cerebras) |
| **Streaming** (`stream: true`) | Very portable | Chunk contents can differ, e.g. whether `usage` arrives in the final chunk |
| **Tool / function calling** | Common, but depends on the model | Small or older models may ignore tools or return malformed arguments |
| **JSON mode / structured outputs** | Common | `json_object` is more widely supported than strict `json_schema`. Cerebras says `tools` combined with `response_format` isn't universally supported |
| **Embeddings** (`/embeddings`) | Patchy | Gemini and Mistral serve embeddings. Groq serves no embedding models. Hugging Face's OpenAI-compatible router is chat-only |
| **Vision** (image input) | Depends on the model | Needs a vision-capable model. Cerebras accepts base64 data URIs only, not HTTPS image URLs |

Some notes from the official docs:

- **Gemini** has the broadest compatibility layer. It covers streaming, function calling, structured output, embeddings (`gemini-embedding-001`), image understanding and even image generation ([source](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai)). Gemini-only parameters go through `extra_body`.
- **Groq** supports `json_object` and strict `json_schema` structured outputs on `openai/gpt-oss-120b` ([structured outputs docs](https://console.groq.com/docs/structured-outputs)). It rejects `logprobs` and `logit_bias`, and it changes `temperature: 0` to `1e-8` ([source](https://console.groq.com/docs/openai)).
- **Cerebras** requires provider-specific options such as `reasoning_format` to go through `extra_body` when you use the OpenAI SDK ([source](https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/resources/openai)).
- **Hugging Face's** router at `router.huggingface.co/v1` is chat completions only. For embeddings you use Hugging Face's own client ([source](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/index)).

In Python, `extra_body` works like this:

```python
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-oss-120b",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Solve 17 * 23."}],
    extra_body={"reasoning_format": "parsed"},  # Cerebras-specific
)
```

If you're building retrieval, the embeddings gap matters most. You may end up using one provider for chat and another for vectors. Our guide to [free LLM APIs for RAG and embeddings](/blog/free-llm-api-for-rag-embeddings/) covers that setup.

## Common errors and how to fix them

The SDKs raise a typed exception for each HTTP status: `AuthenticationError` for 401, `NotFoundError` for 404 and `RateLimitError` for 429 ([openai-python error handling](https://github.com/openai/openai-python#handling-errors)). These three cause almost every failed first request.

### 401 Unauthorized

The provider rejected your key. Common causes:

- **Wrong key for the base URL.** An OpenAI key sent to Groq, or a Groq key sent to Gemini, fails. Check that the key and URL come from the same provider.
- **The base URL didn't apply.** If `OPENAI_BASE_URL` isn't exported in the shell that runs your code, the SDK falls back to `api.openai.com` and sends your Groq key to OpenAI. Print `client.base_url` to check.
- **Stray whitespace or quotes** in the key, often from a copy-paste or a `.env` file.
- **Missing token permissions.** Hugging Face needs a fine-grained token with the "Make calls to Inference Providers" permission ([source](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/index)).

### 404 Not Found / model not found

Either the path or the model is wrong:

- **The base URL is missing part of its path.** `https://api.groq.com/v1` returns a 404. The correct URL is `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`. Copy base URLs exactly.
- **The model ID doesn't exist on that provider.** Model IDs differ between providers. The same weights are `openai/gpt-oss-120b` on Groq and `gpt-oss-120b` on Cerebras.
- **The model was retired.** This one is easy to miss. Groq shut down `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` and `llama-3.1-8b-instant` on its free and developer tiers on August 16, 2026, and recommends `openai/gpt-oss-120b` and `openai/gpt-oss-20b` instead ([Groq deprecations](https://console.groq.com/docs/deprecations)). Tutorials written before then now fail with a model error.
- **The whole service is gone.** GitHub Models, once a popular free OpenAI-compatible endpoint, [was fully retired on July 30, 2026](https://docs.github.com/en/github-models/quickstart). Code pointing at `models.github.ai/inference` needs a new provider.

In each case, call `GET /models` and copy an ID from the response.

### 429 Too Many Requests

You've hit a free-tier limit. That can be requests per minute, requests per day, or tokens per minute. Fixes, in order:

1. **Let the SDK retry.** Both SDKs retry 429s twice by default with exponential backoff. Raise this with `max_retries` (Python) or `maxRetries` (Node).
2. **Read the headers.** Groq, for example, returns `retry-after` in seconds plus `x-ratelimit-remaining-requests` and `x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens` ([source](https://console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits)). Wait that long before you try again.
3. **Send fewer tokens.** Token-per-minute caps are often the tighter limit. Trim prompts and set `max_tokens`.
4. **Fail over to another provider.** This is where the provider map above pays off. Catch `RateLimitError` and retry on the next provider.

```python
import openai

try:
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages)
except openai.RateLimitError:
    client, model = make_client("cerebras")
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages)
```

For the limits per provider, see our [free LLM API rate limits comparison](/blog/free-llm-api-rate-limits-compared/).

## Free OpenAI-compatible providers and base URLs

These seven providers have free access and an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint. The example models are ones each provider's docs or live `/models` endpoint listed in September 2026. Check `GET /models` before you ship, because catalogs change monthly.

| Provider | Base URL | Example model | Docs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Groq](/providers/groq/) | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | [OpenAI compat](https://console.groq.com/docs/openai) |
| [Google Gemini](/providers/google_gemini/) | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/` | `gemini-3.8-flash` | [OpenAI compat](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai) |
| [Cerebras](/providers/cerebras/) | `https://api.cerebras.ai/v1` | `gpt-oss-120b` | [OpenAI compat](https://inference-docs.cerebras.ai/resources/openai) |
| [Mistral AI](/providers/mistral/) | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | `mistral-small-latest` | [Quickstart](https://docs.mistral.ai/getting-started/quickstart) |
| [OpenRouter](/providers/openrouter/) | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `openrouter/free` | [Quickstart](https://openrouter.ai/docs/quickstart) |
| [Hugging Face](/providers/huggingface/) | `https://router.huggingface.co/v1` | `openai/gpt-oss-120b:fastest` | [Inference Providers](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/index) |
| [NVIDIA NIM](/providers/nvidia_nim/) | `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1` | `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | [LLM APIs](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/reference/llm-apis) |

Some of these providers have their own conventions:

- **OpenRouter** marks free variants with a `:free` suffix (for example `qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free`). `openrouter/free` is a router that picks a free model for you. Accounts without purchased credits get 50 free-model requests per day, and buying $10 or more of credits raises that to 1,000 ([OpenRouter FAQ](https://openrouter.ai/docs/faq)).
- **Hugging Face** routes each request to a backend provider. You can add a suffix to the model ID to choose one: `:fastest`, `:cheapest`, or a provider name such as `:groq`.
- **Mistral** accepts `-latest` aliases such as `mistral-small-latest`, which follow the newest release. Use a dated ID like `mistral-small-2506` when you need the model's output to stay the same.

For free-tier details, speeds and card requirements for every compatible provider, see the [full drop-in list](/blog/openai-compatible-free-llm-apis-list/) or [browse the directory](/). For a side-by-side of the two most popular options, read [Groq vs Google Gemini free tier](/blog/groq-vs-google-gemini-free-tier/).

## Quick checklist

Before you conclude that a provider "isn't compatible", check these five things:

1. The base URL is copied in full, including `/openai/v1`, `/v1beta/openai/` or `/api/v1`.
2. The key comes from the same provider as the URL, and nothing else overrides it.
3. The model ID comes from that provider's `GET /models` today, not from an old tutorial.
4. You're using `chat.completions`, not the Responses API or legacy `completions`.
5. Advanced features (tools, JSON schema, vision, embeddings) are confirmed in that provider's docs for that model.

With those five right, an app written against the OpenAI SDK can move between free providers by changing environment variables, with no code changes.
